concepts.label: Metadata Purge Interval (tombstone purge interval)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the per-bucket/per-cluster setting governing how many days elapse before storage:tombstone entries are permanently removed; distinct from storage:tombstone itself (the record) and from data:max-ttl-setting (document expiry, an unrelated axis)

relations.subject: bucket:ephemeral-bucket
relations.evidence: Auto-compaction settings affect on-disk data, and therefore do not apply to Ephemeral buckets.

relations.subject: storage:auto-compaction
relations.evidence: Users with the Full or Cluster administrator roles can configure compaction settings using [the Couchbase Server Web Console](#configure-auto-compaction-with-the-ui), the [command line tools](#configure-auto-compaction-with-the-cli), or the [REST API](#configure-auto-compaction-with-the-rest-api).

relations.subject: storage:auto-compaction
relations.evidence: Users with the Full or Cluster administrator roles can configure compaction settings using [the Couchbase Server Web Console](#configure-auto-compaction-with-the-ui), the [command line tools](#configure-auto-compaction-with-the-cli), or the [REST API](#configure-auto-compaction-with-the-rest-api).

relations.subject: index:memory-optimized-storage
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition, auto-compaction does not apply to memory-optimized index storage.

relations.subject: index:standard-storage
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - specifically for its auto-compaction (Index Fragmentation) settings, not the storage mode itself, which also exists in Enterprise Edition per the already-promoted concept
relations.evidence: The Couchbase Server Community Edition auto-compaction settings contains fields to control [Index Fragmentation](#index-fragmentation). Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition does not have these settings.

relations.subject: storage-engine:couchstore
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the Time Interval field applies only to this storage engine, not to Magma
relations.evidence: This setting only appears for buckets using the Couchstore storage engine. It does not appear for Magma buckets.

relations.subject: bucket:ephemeral-bucket
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the CLUSTER-WIDE default cannot be changed for ephemeral buckets, though a PER-BUCKET override still can be
relations.evidence: Neither the default nor the customized frequency of metadata purges for any Ephemeral bucket is affected by changes made here. Note that although the default interval for Ephemeral buckets is, as with Couchbase buckets, `3`, only _per bucket_ interval-changes can be made, for Ephemeral buckets: the default interval for Ephemeral buckets cannot be changed globally.

relations.subject: storage:metadata-purge-interval
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - loose fit: a too-low setting causes cross-cluster inconsistency rather than a structural cascade; flagged as a judgement call
relations.evidence: If you set this value too low, you may see inconsistent results in Views queries, such as deleted items appearing in a result set. You may also see inconsistent items across clusters, if XDCR has been set up between the clusters.

relations.subject: server/8.0/manage/manage-settings/configure-compact-settings
relations.evidence: For information on providing customized settings, see [Create a Bucket](../manage-buckets/create-bucket.md) and [Edit a Bucket](../manage-buckets/edit-bucket.md).

notable_absence.finding: The page states 'If the metadata purge interval is set too low, it can also cause severe issues with transactions, especially for ephemeral buckets' - a stated INTERACTION between storage:metadata-purge-interval and n1ql:transactions/server:distributed-acid-transactions that is specific to ephemeral buckets, distinct from every other bucket-type exclusion in this batch (which are about what a setting can BE, not what breaks when a shared setting is misconfigured). Not turned into a relation because the mechanism connecting a too-low purge interval to transaction failure is never explained on this page, and a bare cascadesTo/doesNotSupport triple would overstate what is actually a caution rather than a stated causal mechanism.

cross_component_finding: This page directly corroborates the round's central hypothesis at cluster-settings scope, not just at per-bucket-setting scope: 'Auto-compaction settings affect on-disk data, and therefore do not apply to Ephemeral buckets' is a total, unqualified exclusion (not a choice among a smaller set of options, as with ejection or durability) - the most complete bucket-type-gated exclusion found in this batch. Combined with edit-bucket.md's Storage-Backend/Encryption-At-Rest gates and create-bucket.md's durability-list gate, this batch now has FOUR independent, differently-shaped confirmations that bucket TYPE (not edition, not storage engine choice) is the governing axis for disk-persistence-dependent capability.
